newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens stronger amid U.S. dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens stronger amid U.S. dlr gains.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened firmer on Tuesday at C$1.3671 (US$0.7315) in quiet trade. * Dealers said strength in the U.S. dollar overnight spilled over into the Canadian currency. * Strength of U.S. economic data seen setting the direction for Canadian currency over the near term, strengthening trend for Canadian dollar seen likely to continue.
Dealers said the market is now focusing on this week's stream of U.S. economic reports and their effect on the U.S. dollar versus other major currencies.

While strong U.S. reports could strengthen the big dollar, which would benefit Canada, they may also raise the prospect of another U.S. rate hike. Concern about this could weaken the Canadian dollar past C$1.37 (US$0.7299). However, dealers said a strengthening trend is more likely.
"The view is we'll try to take out the 200-day moving average at C$1.3655 with a potential extension towards the very strong technical level of C$1.3615," said Wateridge.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose against the German mark to 1.3137 marks from 1.3127 marks at Monday's close. It rose to 83.66 Japanese yen from 83.18 yen at Monday's close.
